utterances.text: And currently on the Epic side, we have some feature requests coming in both from users and customers that they are looking for more attributes to be updatable in bulk for list of Epics. Currently only labels are supported when it comes to bulk editing Epics. We can add support for more attributes as long as there's a private API available, but then we are basically introducing technical debt because Pages GraphQL and we are using REST for new features.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: So we, we had this conversation over a year ago when we rewrote issues list in GraphQL. So I have linked the epic where it was proposed first, like lack of mutations available. We have also created a similar epic for work items, which is here. And it basically tracks the same effort for work item.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: So in case we want to support bulk editing of attributes, then you would need to start thinking about having the mutations first in GraphiQL.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: Ian, you want to verbalize your point there?

utterances.speaker: D
utterances.text: Yeah, just a minor thought that when we add bulk editing of work items, we will need to think about how to bulk edit work items of different types because each type may not have all the attributes you need to update. So this is something to clarify, but It depends on priorities.

utterances.speaker: D
utterances.text: If we need GraphQL API endpoint for epic and issues sooner, we might need to add

utterances.speaker: D
utterances.text: endpoint for bulk editing epics and issues now before we support work items. So it might be two different things.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: Yeah, so Marcin, regarding your question that does this influence, uh, the UI, so for now, as, uh, until we add the backend first, as far as like creating mutations are required, there isn't any, uh, UI update that is going to take place. First we need to have mutations that support bulk editing.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: Once the mutations are in, then we can add UI on top of it. I, I believe that if we add mutations to update issues list in bulk, uh, then we can keep the existing UI as it is. It would be a behind-the-scenes change where we remove the REST API usage and replace it with GraphQL. The sidebar behavior for bulk editing will remain unchanged. Same thing goes for epics as well.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: UI updates will only take place when we start adding new attribute types to that bulk edit sidebar.

utterances.speaker: C
utterances.text: Cool.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: G
utterances.text: Yeah, so the last item. So feel free to start the discussion in both the epics that I've linked there if you have any thoughts. And the second item was already answered by Brett, so we can skip it. It was around DB schema determining items for work items. Next one is John.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Yeah, quick one.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Last chance to vote on what time this meeting should be moved to. Please check out the issue. There are multiple options. All the context is in the issue. You probably know it by now. So yeah, please take a look and vote if you haven't already. I'll probably try and wrap it up today so that everyone has 2 weeks to adjust to the new time.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Nicholas, really?

utterances.speaker: K
utterances.text: Just a fun comment because Donald needs to wake up at 5:30 AM. I'm not sure

utterances.speaker: K
utterances.text: if this is the move. If you move it to 13:30 UTC, this will be very early for you.

utterances.speaker: C
utterances.text: That's okay. I can— I won't have camera on and I'll probably take it from home if that's the case. But the— I normally go to the APAC, uh, one anyway, so there's no need for me to be active in both, I don't think. So don't keep it at the current time on for my sake, essentially.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Yeah, it's a good point. I think that's reasonable, right? Like, we should try to make it so that everyone can at least attend one of the two meetings. Um, and so if I'm looking at the votes and it's a tiebreak, um, if everyone thinks that's Thanks, that's fair. I'll use that to break the tie, basically. Like, if somebody's able to make both, right? I'll bias towards the one where it includes more people in at least one of the meetings.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: That said, there is an option to like veto anytime. So if you definitely absolutely do not want, there's a third emoji for that. Reaction. If you just really, really detest a particular time of day, you can express your opinion on the issue. Anyway, this is going on too long. It's just a vote. Like, feel free to take a look.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: All right, Amanda, I think you're up.

utterances.speaker: F
utterances.text: Yeah, I just want to say I've worked on a number of cross-team projects in the past, and I've never seen one executed— that's not the right word—

utterances.speaker: F
utterances.text: I haven't seen one delivered in such a really impressive way. The collaboration between the teams and the bias for delivery and the bias for demoing and just getting something usable out there so that we can keep pushing forward is really, really impressive. I'm like proud to be part of this team.

utterances.speaker: F
utterances.text: Thanks so much to everybody who's working on the OKR project.

utterances.speaker: H
utterances.text: If there are no other points, I see that Rudy joined the meeting, so maybe we can circle back to point 1.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: So he has. Rudy, are you there?

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: I am. How are you?

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: How's it going? So you're very welcome. Uh, we did a short introduction for you earlier, but you weren't here, but that's fine, it's not expected. Uh, so maybe you could tell us a bit about yourself, um, where you were before GitLab, and, uh, yeah, why you decided to join, where you're located, and what you like to do for fun outside work.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Yes, I'm Rudy. I'm based in New York City. Uh, before GitLab, I was at RE/MAX I was the lead frontend developer on a tool called Megaphone, which is basically just a tool for— an internal marketing tool for Remax real estate agents. I joined GitLab just because I think it's the right place to view developers, period. And I wanted to be part of that.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: And yeah, outside of work, I enjoy spending time with my family, my young 2-year-old daughter. I watch sports all the time, working out, and Yeah, I'm glad to be here. Very excited to be here.

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: Thank you to all.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Awesome, you're very welcome.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: Okay, that was our last, uh, agenda item, so I'm going to stop recording. But, uh, I think we have some social time items, but this is not for the benefit of people on YouTube.
